newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Congress panel approves FEF extension.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Congress panel approves FEF extension.

text.p: A committee in Brazil's Chamber of Deputies approved Wednesday a bill extending until 1999 the government's Fiscal Stabilization Fund (FEF), a key tool in its battle to keep public spending under control.
A congressional official said the bill was approved by the committee in a show of hands although amendments had yet to be put to a vote.
The FEF allows the federal government to hold on to about $26 billion each year in receipts earmarked by the constitutition for spending by states and municipalities.
The money is used to cover shortfalls in the federal budget and the remainder is passed on to local governments.

A first version of the fund introduced in 1994 ran until the end of 1995. In March last year, a new version was launched. It is due to expire June 30, although the bill currently in Congress will be retroactive to avoid a break in the system.

Leaders of government-allied parties and representatives of state and municipal authorities, who had been at loggerheads over the bill, reached an agreement earlier today, paving the way for the committee-level vote.

Under the agreement, the share of the FEF to be passed on to local governments this year was raised to 50 percent from the 40 percent originally in the bill. The share rises to 60 percent in 1998 and 80 percent in 1999.
The bill now advances to the floor of the Chamber of Deputies where, as a constitutional amendment, it requires two three-fifths majorities. It must also be approved in the Senate.
